title: Computational Primitive Specification
abstract: This document defines the universal vocabulary that every CHOIR reasoning system uses, regardless of domain §0 . It states a seven-condition admission test that a candidate primitive must pass, applies that test to the candidates named in the research brief, and records which pass, which are demoted to composites, and which remain contested §0, §3, §4, §6 . The source calls the Influence/Causation split — Influence being second-order modulation, Causation first-order production — "the primitive set's most consequential departure from standard rule engines," and the demotion of Rule to a composite "the least intuitive result of applying the admission test" §7, §4 . Status note. This publication carries the status Active : the underlying document is drafted but has not been accepted as specification. The source itself is marked "Draft for review" in Phase 1 — Computational Foundations. choir/research/README.md records the programme-level position: "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." MANIFESTO.md itself states the underlying formulation — "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth." Nothing below should be read as an approved ruling.

title: Reasoning Ontology
abstract: This document specifies how CHOIR's computational primitives are organised §1 : a three-layer architecture L0 Meta / L1 Core / L2 Domain with dependencies pointing upward only, a four-way entity hierarchy, seven relationship families with explicitly declared algebraic properties, two separate inheritance systems, a namespace and versioning scheme, and nine validation checks the ontology must pass against itself §2–§8, summarised at §11 . The ontology being designed is an ontology of reasoning, not of any subject matter — it contains no grahas, no statutes, no diagnoses; those live in domain layers that attach to it §1, §6 . The source carries the status "Draft for review": it is drafted but not accepted as specification , and per MANIFESTO.md — as the source itself states at §8 — the ontology is a hypothesis and needs its own acceptance tests.

title: Knowledge Graph Specification
abstract: This document fixes the shape of CHOIR's knowledge store. It derives three requirements — statement-level metadata, edges as edge targets, and native n-ary relations — assesses RDF triples, labelled property graphs, hypergraphs, semantic networks and knowledge graph embeddings against them, and decides on a typed, directed, role-labelled hypergraph as the model of record with an LPG projection and an RDF-star export §1–§3 . It specifies node and hyperedge schemas, an index set chosen for rule matching, and twelve machine-checkable store invariants §4–§6 . The source carries the status "Draft for review". This publication is Active: the research document is drafted but not accepted as specification. choir/research/README.md records the programme-level position — "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md " — where MANIFESTO.md itself states the underlying formulation as " t reat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth". The source document itself does not cite MANIFESTO.md for its own status. It records that it "only fixes the shape " §4.3 , that physical realisation is " n ot decided here" §8 , and — in its single citation of MANIFESTO.md , which is to scope — that "implementation is deliberately deferred" §8 .

title: Vedic Reasoning Methodology
abstract: This document studies the inferential machinery of classical Jyotiṣa texts — what counts as a reason, how rules compose, what defeats what, and how conflict is settled §0.1 . Its central finding is that the tradition supplies its own conflict-resolution and explanation machinery, drawn from Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā and Vyākaraṇa, and that this machinery is more precisely specified than what most modern rule engines ship with; CHOIR does not need to invent these mechanisms, it needs to formalise them §1 . The analysis closes by deriving thirteen numbered computational requirements R1–R13 that the corpus imposes on the rest of the system §7 . This document carries the status Active : it is a research document, drafted but not accepted as specification . The source itself is marked "Draft for review". Per choir/research/README.md , all 18 research deliverables are drafted, none accepted, and every document is a hypothesis.

title: Sanskrit Analysis Pipeline
abstract: This document specifies a nine-stage pipeline S0–S8 for analysing Sanskrit śāstric verse into the CHOIR ambiguity-preserving intermediate representation, governed by a single principle: ambiguity is preserved as a lattice of ranked alternatives until evidence bearing on it is available, and pruning flows backward from later stages to earlier ones §1, §2 . It asserts as "the load-bearing insight of the whole pipeline" that kāraka roles map directly onto the role-labelled participants of a CHOIR hyperedge — the grammatical analysis becomes the storage structure rather than being translated away §6.4 — and heads its anuvṛtti cross-verse inheritance stage "the stage that is usually missing": a scope-resolution stage whose failure mode is a silent, well-formed, over-general rule §7, §11 . Both are design positions; the source reports no measured results. The document is carried at status Active : it is drafted but not accepted as specification . Per choir/research/README.md , all 18 research deliverables are drafted and none accepted: "Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." Its own status line reads "Draft for review".

title: Shloka Compiler
abstract: This document specifies the six transformations that carry a Sanskrit verse to an executable rule, and states what each one preserves and what it loses §1 . It argues that translation is a validation artefact generated from the analysis rather than a stage in the compilation path §3 , that anuvṛtti resolution is exactly scope resolution and cross-reference resolution is exactly linking — in both cases unresolved references are errors, not warnings §5.2, §6.2 — and that unresolved ambiguity is a first-class compiler output emitted for scholar adjudication rather than guessed at §1.1, §7 . The source document is marked Status: Draft for review and is published here as an Active research document: drafted, but not accepted as specification . The document-level statement of that condition is made by choir/research/README.md : "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." MANIFESTO.md itself states the rule at the level of objects rather than documents: "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Rule Extraction Framework
abstract: This document specifies how rules are extracted from śāstric verse into CHOIR: a canonical rule schema with mandatory and derived fields §2 , a Mīmāṃsā-based gate that decides which verses are rules at all §4 , a dual independent extraction protocol with adjudication and a contested outcome §5 , two orthogonal confidence axes set at extraction time §6 , a deliberately conservative unification policy §7 , and acceptance metrics against a gold set §8 . Its governing definition of consistency is that two competent analysts working independently from the same source produce rules that agree on structure, scope, and conclusion — or disagree in a way the framework makes visible and adjudicable §1 . The source document is carried in the repository as Status: Draft for review ; per choir/research/README.md , all 18 research deliverables are drafted, none is accepted, and every document is a hypothesis. This document is drafted but not accepted as specification.

title: Canonical Shloka Analysis (Benchmark)
abstract: This document carries a single half-verse stating the formation of Gajakesarī yoga end to end through every layer of the CHOIR pipeline — original Sanskrit, word-by-word analysis, grammar, meaning, reasoning structure, extracted rule, reasoning-language form, execution, and explanation — and fixes that worked example as the project's reference benchmark against which any pipeline change is validated §1 . It records fifteen acceptance criteria B1–B15 that a pipeline must reproduce, of which B5, B9 and B13 are identified as discriminating §11 . It also records that the verse's citation is unverified: the rule carries diagnostic E-ATTEST , cannot enter the authoritative corpus, and is admitted only as a methodological benchmark §1.2, §7 . Status note. This document is Active: it is a complete research document, drafted, and not accepted as specification . The source itself is marked "Draft for review" § header . choir/research/README.md records the programme-level position — "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." MANIFESTO.md itself states the underlying commitment as "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Evidence Model
abstract: The document specifies how CHOIR represents an evidence item, how evidence items are typed by pramāṇa , and how they are aggregated in support of a claim §2, §3, §4 . Its central commitment is that evidence items are not independent, and that treating them as if they were is "the dominant source of overconfidence in rule-based systems" §1 — so aggregation runs over an independence partition rather than over an item list §4.4 , with defeasible structure settled before any grading is applied §5.1 . The source carries its own status line, Draft for review ; this publication is drafted but not accepted as specification, and per MANIFESTO.md every research document is a hypothesis.

title: Conflict Resolution
abstract: This document specifies how CHOIR detects, classifies, and resolves disagreement between rules: a seven-class conflict taxonomy §3 , a context-splitting step applied before any precedence reasoning §4 , a partial-order precedence scheme drawn from utsarga/apavāda , Pāṇinian metarules and Mīmāṃsā interpretive ordering §5 , well-foundedness requirements for defeater chains §6 , and six resolution outcomes including vikalpa — a terminal disjunction — and escalation §7 . Its governing commitment is that the system must never silently pick a winner, and that "unresolved" is a legitimate output §1 . The source carries the status Draft for review and is published here as Active : it is a complete research document that has been drafted but not accepted as specification . choir/research/README.md records the programme-level position: "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." MANIFESTO.md itself states the underlying formulation as "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Confidence Framework
abstract: The source document specifies how CHOIR computes and reports confidence: as a three-axis vector — extraction, interpretive, inferential — derived from evidence structure rather than authored by any human, and summarised by the minimum of the three axes rather than by a product or an average §1, §3.4 . It names six anti-patterns it holds to be wrong §5 , states plainly that for Jyotiṣa there is no outcome ground truth and that the calibration target must therefore be textual fidelity rather than prediction §7.1 , and closes with six unresolved questions, including whether confidence should be computed ordinally or numerically at all §9 . This publication is Active: the source document is drafted but not accepted as specification . Its own header records its status as "Draft for review," and per MANIFESTO.md every research document is a hypothesis — the manifesto's instruction is to treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth.

title: Explainability Framework
abstract: This document establishes that CHOIR explanations are projections of the execution record — never regenerated, paraphrased, or reconstructed by a separate process — and that faithfulness therefore holds by construction rather than by evaluation §1 . It specifies the seven mandatory components of an explanation §2 , adopts the Nyāya pañcāvayava as the explanation schema §3 , defines the trace as a DAG with a replay guarantee §4 , fixes four audience renderings as views over one trace §6 , and lists eight verification tests §9 . The source carries the status "Draft for review" and records six open questions, including one it states outright is "not solved here" §10.6 . Status note. This publication has status Active : the research document is complete and drafted, but it has not been accepted as specification. Per MANIFESTO.md , every research document is a hypothesis. Nothing below should be read as a governing ruling.

title: CHOIR Intermediate Representation
abstract: This document specifies a three-level intermediate representation — HIR, MIR, LIR — that sits between CHOIR's source-text front end and its matching, evidence, conflict, and explanation machinery §1, §2 . Its central claim is that three requirements the source calls unusual — representable unresolved ambiguity, structural provenance to a source span, and defeat modelled as an attack on an inference edge rather than a weight on a node — drive the whole design, and that MIR is the layer at which the domain-independence claim is tested §2, §2.2 . Of the three, the source claims outright novelty for only one: "U1 is the one no conventional IR has" §1 . The source carries the status "Draft for review" ; it is a complete research document, drafted, and is not accepted as specification . choir/research/README.md records the programme-level position — all 18 deliverables drafted, none accepted, every document a hypothesis — citing MANIFESTO.md , whose own formulation is to " t reat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Reasoning Language (CRL)
abstract: This document specifies CRL — the CHOIR Reasoning Language — as the human-facing surface syntax for MIR, giving its design constraints, an EBNF grammar, worked examples in three domains, a type system, an explicit list of what the language cannot express, and a formal semantics §1–§8 . It discharges a debt recorded in knowledge graph spec.md §4.3: choosing a hypergraph means CHOIR inherits no formal semantics and must supply its own §7 . The source carries the status "Draft for review" and records six open questions of its own, including that its primary design constraint — reviewability by non-programmers — is untested §9 . Status note. This document is Active: it is a complete research document, drafted, and not accepted as specification . Per choir/research/README.md , every document in this series is a hypothesis — all 18 deliverables drafted, none accepted. Nothing below should be read as a governing ruling.

title: Execution Pipeline
abstract: This document specifies the ten-stage execution pipeline that runs compiled CHOIR rules against domain data, expanding the pipeline given in the brief by two inserted stages — derived-fact computation and saturation — both inserted "for correctness rather than convenience" §1 . Its central commitment is that every applicable rule fires before any adjudication begins §4.2 , which the document identifies as "the pipeline's most consequential design decision and the one most likely to be questioned on performance grounds" §4.2 . It further specifies the determinism contract and execution record §7 , incremental invalidation §8 , human-in-the-loop entry points §9 , performance cost drivers §11 , and a failure-mode table whose unifying principle is that "an unevaluated thing is never treated as a false thing" §12 . The source document carries the status "Draft for review". This publication is Active : the source is a complete research document, drafted but not accepted as specification . Per choir/research/README.md , all 18 research deliverables in this programme are drafted and none accepted — "Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." The manifesto's own formulation is narrower: "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Domain Independence
abstract: The source document states, and then tests, the claim that the same compiler, IR, and execution pipeline serve Jyotiṣa, law, medicine, finance and engineering, with domain variation confined to vocabulary, kernels, and parameters §1 . It maps every L1 primitive across five domains §2 , defines a portability metric §6 , and records a measured result of portability 1.00 against an executable prototype across four domains with an engineering hold-out control §6.1 . The document is explicit that the result is bounded: the prototype exercises a subset of the MIR, and the falsifiers F3 graded defeat , F6 influence collapsing into weighted causation and F7 cross-domain precedence remain open or untested §6.2, §7 . This publication is Active : the source is a complete research document, drafted but not accepted as specification. Its own header records its status as "Draft for review". Per MANIFESTO.md , every research document is a hypothesis rather than an established truth.

title: Computational Symbolism Review
abstract: The source document surveys the symbolic-AI tradition CHOIR sits in and then states "precisely where CHOIR differs, and where it does not " §1 . It records that almost every individual mechanism in CHOIR already exists in the literature, tabulates nine such mechanisms against their prior art, lists seven things CHOIR does not claim §3 , and reduces the novelty claim to six specific differences §4 plus a composition claim §5 , each stated with the observation that would refute it. The document is explicit that the composition claim "is a design claim, not a theoretical result, and it is unvalidated" §5 , that the survey is analytical rather than a systematic literature review §7 , and that one of its own threats — influence reducing to weighted causation — remains open §6, T4 . This publication is Active : the source is a complete research document, drafted but not accepted as specification. Its own header records its status as "Draft for review". Per MANIFESTO.md , every research document is a hypothesis rather than an established truth.

title: Related Work Survey
abstract: The source document assesses twelve families of existing system — Cyc, OpenCog, SOAR, ACT-R, Drools, Prolog, OWL/RDF/SPARQL, Neo4j, LegalRuleML, Catala, truth maintenance systems, and computational Sanskrit — against nine axes chosen because they are CHOIR's requirements §1 , and records, for most of them, where CHOIR differs and what CHOIR takes §2 . The treatment is not uniform: a "What CHOIR takes" block appears for six of the twelve sections, and §2.9 and §2.12 replace the standard "How CHOIR differs" heading with an "Honest assessment" and a "Limits for CHOIR" note respectively. It concludes with a conservatively stated positioning — CHOIR as "a compiler architecture for interpretive normative corpora " occupying the gap between computational linguistics and rule engines §5 — and a six-item verification queue that must be discharged before any external novelty claim is made §4 . The document states its own limits plainly: it is "an analytical survey drawn from the established landscape of these systems, not a systematic literature review", version-level capabilities have not been verified against current documentation §1 , and the comparison is "comparison against a design" rather than against a running system §3, §5 . This publication is Active : the source is a complete research document, drafted but not accepted as specification. Its own header records its status as "Draft for review". choir/research/README.md records the programme position: "All 18 deliverables drafted. None accepted. Every document is a hypothesis, per MANIFESTO.md ." The formulation MANIFESTO.md itself gives is at the level of the computational object: "Treat every computational object as a hypothesis rather than an established truth."

title: Reasoning Execution Substrate
abstract: This document records the approved ruling on what executes a reasoning kernel: deterministic code, or a language model constrained by an output schema. The ruling adopts Option A — deterministic kernels are the architecture, and the model-backed path under applications/investment/prototype risk rik/ is legacy, retained for reference and not canonical architecture § Recommendation, § Consequences . The source records that the decision was written down retrospectively, after the repository already contained two contradictory answers to the question status note . This is a Published ruling: approved by Piyush on 2026-08-04 § Approval Status .

title: Document Intake for the Vertical Slice
abstract: This decision fixes what a "document" is for v0.1 of the investment vertical slice, and what the parsing layer in front of the CHOIR intermediate representation is permitted to do to it. It approves Option A — the document is the packet, serialised — under which parsing is deserialisation plus structural validation, with no extraction, no inference, and no defaulting § Options, § Recommendation . The source records the ruling as "Approved 2026-08-06, and broadened" , with product-generated serialised packet documents approved on the same terms and one binding principle: "Documents may represent packets. They may not interpret them." § Approval Status .

title: Product Application Architecture
abstract: This document records the approved architecture for the product application built around the CHOIR reasoning engine. It answers four questions — where the product lives and what it is called §1 , what vocabulary it uses §2 , how it obtains a judgment given the engine is frozen §3 , and where institutional state lives §4 — and rules the scope conflict between CHOIR v0.1 RESEARCH FREEZE.md §5 and the product instruction. All four choices were approved on 2026-08-06, together with the ruling that §5's engineering exclusions apply to the reasoning engine and not to product layers.

title: Judgment Supersession
abstract: This document records an approved and implemented architecture ruling: institutional history is append-only, and a committee decision remains permanently bound to the exact judgment that existed when that decision was recorded § Ruling . It was ruled by the architect in response to a verified defect in which re-running an analysis overwrote a judgment record in place, leaving a ledger entry pointing at a digest nothing on disk matched § Decision . The ruling selects supersession over the alternatives of archiving and freezing, and the source records the resulting data model, invariants, tests, and costs § Options put to the architect, § Implementation, § Invariants, and where they are defended, § Consequences .

title: Canonical Definition of DAALE
abstract: This ADR records that the question what DAALE is was open and deliberately left unanswered, and that no implementation was permitted to depend on any assumption about DAALE until the ADR was accepted stated in the unheaded status paragraph that opens the source . It records five accounts of DAALE — drawn from the repository, the research corpus and two independent architectural reviews — which the source states "do not agree, and each has been treated as authoritative by someone," and records that the modules named in the last of those accounts do not exist in this repository. The conclusion the source draws from that verification is hedged: the review is "a competent analysis of a different or hypothetical DAALE," and "that is not a criticism of it — its diagnosis of the missing canonical semantics converges with this repository's own recorded governance gap" § "Why it is open" . This ADR no longer governs. Per the governance block ruled 2026-08-22, DECISION-005 is INVALIDATED — not approved and not rejected, because "the question was never answered, the decision was retired" — and its replacement ruling is recorded as "not yet recorded" § "Current governance", § "Governance record" . No replacement is on record; the evaluator boundary in daale/ therefore stands unchanged until a superseding architectural artifact exists.

title: The Material Snapshot Layer
abstract: This decision introduces Material Snapshot : "the immutable institutional material a judgment was formed from, identified by a material digest computed at full institutional fidelity in the product layer" § "Decision" . It was motivated by a measured digest collision in which two materially different diligence packs produced one identical reasoning-record hash, so that a real change to what an institution claimed about its own evidence produced no new judgment § "The defect that motivated it" . The source records the layer as "the first immutable institutional identity layer" — "Everything future provenance work depends on sits on top of this" — and its status as Approved 2026-08-06 Authorizations 1–4, 6, 7 . Implemented.

title: The Candidate Escalation Rule
abstract: This decision fixes which candidate origins may commit directly to canonical state and which are escalated to REVIEW REQUIRED . The rule is stated as an allow-list of three deterministic origins — dcore , rfabric , algorithm — with everything else escalating; the source states that the allow-list form "is the whole substance of the decision rather than a stylistic choice" § "The property that matters: default-deny" . The document carries Status: Approved 2026-08-14 , codified by the architect's DAALE v0 closure instruction, and supersedes assumption G3 in docs/development/IMPLEMENTATION LOG.md for the DAALE v0 Phases 1–2 cycle § preamble, § "Approval Status" .

title: Constitutional Distillation Protocol
abstract: The Constitutional Distillation Protocol CDP is proposed as a CHOIR primitive for converting explicit institutional governance into implicit specialist behavior, so that specialist kernels behave as though constitutional rules are permanently present rather than receiving those rules as a prompt on every inference § Abstract . The proposal extends prompt distillation from task-specific rule compression into what the source calls institutional reasoning preservation, with the stated result that "governance becomes part of model behavior rather than runtime prompt overhead" § Abstract . It is a research proposal: it defines a five-stage protocol, a two-layer architecture, three hypotheses, four CHOIR-specific evaluation metrics, and three limitations, and it reports no results against any of them.
